english_title: Cauchy Criterion for Pointwise Convergence of Function Sequences
statement_en: A sequence of functions $f_n(x):X\to \mathbb{C}$ converges pointwise to a function $f(x):X\to \mathbb{C}$ if and only if for every fixed $x_0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a positive integer $N_{\varepsilon,x_0}$ such that for all $n,m>N_{\varepsilon,x_0}$, $$|f_n(x_0)-f_m(x_0)|<\varepsilon.$$
key_techniques: reduce to the scalar Cauchy criterion pointwise
fix a point $x_0$ and apply sequence convergence
callout_body: 函数列$f_n(x):X\to \mathbb{C}$逐点收敛到函数$f(x):X\to \mathbb{C}$当且仅当对于任意固定的$x_0$以及任意的$\varepsilon>0$存在正整数$N_{\varepsilon,x_0}$使得任意$n,m>N_{\varepsilon,x_0}$都成立$$|f_n(x_0)-f_m(x_0)|<\varepsilon$$
